Fixed. `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now gives `

`, the same as the unescaped input. **Cause:** a backslash escape like `\"` is replaced with a placeholder during inline parsing. The placeholder was turned back into the character by `UnescapePostprocessor`, which ran on the finished HTML string, after the serializer had already escaped attributes. So the bare `"` went straight into `alt="…"`. Smarty adds `"` and `'` to the escapable characters, which is why it only showed up with that extension. **Library changes:** - **`markdown/treeprocessors.py`:** new `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, registered last (priority 0). It restores escaped characters in element text, tails and attribute values before serialization, so the serializer escapes them like any other text. Code elements are skipped. - **`markdown/postprocessors.py`:** `UnescapePostprocessor` is no longer registered and now raises a deprecation warning. The class is kept so third-party code doesn't break. - **`markdown/inlinepatterns.py`:** raw inline HTML is stored outside the tree, so the new processor never sees it. `HtmlInlineProcessor` now restores escapes when it stores the HTML, so `` still comes out unchanged. - **`markdown/extensions/toc.py`:** switched to the new class so it doesn't raise the deprecation warning. **Behaviour change:** `\>` in normal text now renders as `>` instead of a bare `>`. It's the same fix and valid HTML either way, but the expected output in `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` had to be updated. I noted this in the 3.4 release notes and updated the processor tables in `docs/extensions/api.md`. **Tests added:** - `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` (new): escaped quotes in image alt text, link titles, plain text and raw HTML. The alt-text and link-title tests fail without the fix. - `test_inline_html_backslash_escapes` in `test_raw_html.py` and `test_escaped_chars_in_alt` in `test_images.py`. - `TestUnescapePostprocessor` in `test_apis.py`: the old class still works but warns, and the new processor is the one registered. **Results:** all new and affected tests pass. The full suite (run with `unittest`) has 8 failures, the same 8 as before my changes, so nothing new broke. `pytest tests` on the whole directory doesn't get past collection because of a `TestSuite` class in `test_md_in_html.py`; that was already the case, and targeted pytest runs work fine. flake8 isn't installed in the venv, so the code wasn't linted. Nothing is committed.
